messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT: Elevated packet loss observed across multipath fabric in cluster-prod-rack-7. Impact: distributed serving requests failing with upstream timeouts and container restarts. Pager ID: P-44512

raj-pd: oncall here, seeing >15% packet loss on ibx interfaces around 10:12 UTC. Pager shows many CUDA OOMs after nodes get delayed responses. I'm paged.

anna-sre: looking. getting a bunch of `gdrmx` retransmit logs and `mlx5` errors in dmesg on node gpu-node-74.

sam-runtime: logs from serving show repeated `kvcache` stalls then `std::bad_alloc`/OOM in the runtime, followed by container crashloop. Example: 

```
2026-03-15T10:11:58Z serve[pid=2145]: KVCache::wait_timeout key=... took 1200ms
2026-03-15T10:12:03Z serve[pid=2145]: ERR nvml: OutOfMemory while allocating 2048MB
2026-03-15T10:12:03Z containerd: oom_kill cgroup memory limit exceeded
```

maya-platform: the fabric metrics show a sudden ECN spike and multipath rebalancing at 10:11. Some paths went silent. Could be switch churn or fabric link flap.

raj-pd: ok initial triage plan: 1) isolate affected nodes, 2) failover traffic to dedicated non-sharded pools, 3) reduce request batch sizes, 4) if nodes misbehave, evict and reboot. Can Anna take lead on node isolation? I'll coordinate customer comms.

anna-sre: on it. starting with node gpu-node-74 and gpu-node-75. running `ssh gpu-node-74 sudo dmesg | tail -n 50` now.

anna-sre: dmesg snippet: `mlx5_core 0000:05:00.0: mlx5v2: SRQ err: qp 12345: CQE with bad opcode`, then link down events. also seeing `mlx5_core reset adapter` around the same time.

sam-runtime: while nodes were flapping we automatically fell back to single-shard serving which increased memory pressure per worker; that's why OOMs followed network stalls. We need to prevent fallback to the big single replica. Add a temporary policy to prefer degraded throughput rather than merging shards.

maya-platform: I can push a routing change to prefer regional spare-pool-2 for affected customers. That should cut cross-rack traffic and reduce multipath load. Want me to flip it?

raj-pd: flip it. call out affected customers in comms (we'll start with the top 5 by QPS).

deploy-bot: @raj-pd deploy job started: route-change/2026-03-15T10:18 -> applying to prod.

anna-sre: draining gpu-node-74: `kubectl drain gpu-node-74 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` then cordon. moving workloads off.

sam-runtime: dropping batch_size from 64 -> 8 for live-serving workers in pool-1 to reduce per-request mem. command: `redwoodctl config set pool-1 --batch-size=8 --reason "fabric degradation"`

raj-pd: customer impact: error rate spiked to ~18% for ~7 minutes for model-generation endpoints. Latency p95 doubled for clients hitting pool-1. No confirmed data exfiltration. Logging flags set for high fidelity.

anna-sre: after draining, node gpu-node-74 still shows link flaps. I recommend rebooting kernel/drivers. will cordon and reboot via BMC.

maya-platform: route-change applied. Traffic on spare-pool-2 up by 60%, error rate on main pool trending down to 3%. Good.

sam-runtime: rolling restart for runtime on spare nodes to ensure KV cache warms fast: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/serve-runtime -n prod --selector=pool=spare-pool-2`

anna-sre: BMC reboot scheduled for gpu-node-74. rebooting now. will follow up with health check: `ip -s link show mlx5_*` and `ibstat`.

sam-runtime: note: we saw `cuda: GPU reset required` in logs just before OOMs on one machine. Likely the timeout from RDMA caused huge requeues and memory growth in the serving runtime.

raj-pd: assigning incident roles: incident lead = raj-pd, infrastructure = anna-sre, runtime = sam-runtime, platform routing = maya-platform. I'll open incident ticket and start customer notifications.

pagerbot: Incident created: INC-2026-03-15-44512. Priority P1. Postmortem owner suggested: anna-sre.

anna-sre: node gpu-node-74 is back online after BMC cycle. IB link is still flapping intermittently but fewer drops. Switching NIC firmware to fallback version on that node as next step.

maya-platform: I've scheduled a controlled reschedule of some long-tail jobs off rack-7 to reduce background traffic.

sam-runtime: we pushed config to disallow shard-merge fallback for 20m window: `redwoodctl policy set --no-shard-merge --duration=20m`

raj-pd: customer comms draft: "We experienced increased request errors and latency for a subset of customers between 10:11-10:20 UTC due to an internal network fabric issue causing node restarts. We routed traffic to spares and reduced batch sizes to stabilize. Full details will follow." Approve?

anna-sre: approve. add note about mitigation: drained and rebooted affected nodes, firmware fallback applied, and routing changed.

maya-platform: monitoring shows error rate back <1% for most customers. A few large customers still seeing elevated latency; I'm opening support tickets.

raj-pd: handoff to oncall followup: anna-sre will run postmortem and confirm firmware rollbacks and switch-level diagnostics tomorrow. sam-runtime, please write up runtime memory pattern and why fallback bumped OOMs.

sam-runtime: will collect heap traces and KV cache metrics and drop them in the ticket.

anna-sre: I'm creating the postmortem draft now - including timeline, mitigation, and followups (switch vendor to investigate, NIC fw roll-forward test, routing rules to avoid single-shard fallback).

raj-pd: great. Closing the page. If anything regresses ping me directly. :thumbsup:
